chunks: Safwan narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in the Mosque of Ghadīr Khumm during the day while I was traveling. He said, "Pray in it, for indeed there is merit in it, and my father عليه السلام used to command that."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being asked about
key_terms.بِالنَّهَارِ: during the day, specifying the time mentioned in the question
key_terms.غَدِيرِ خُمٍّ: Ghadir Khumm, the sacred location referred to in the narration
key_terms.فَضْلًا: merit or special virtue associated with the place
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ: mosque, the place in which the prayer is performed
key_terms.مُسَافِرٌ: traveler, describing the legal state of the questioner
key_terms.يَأْمُرُ: used to command, indicating established instruction from the Imam's father عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: Is it recommended to pray in the Mosque of Ghadir Khumm while traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith states that performing salat (prayer) in the Mosque of Ghadir Khumm is recommended even for a traveler during the day. The Imam عليه السلام affirms its special merit and attributes this practice to the instruction of his father عليه السلام.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3143 - It is narrated by Safwan from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

"I asked Abu Ibrahim (as) about praying in the Mosque of Ghadir Khumm during the day while I am traveling.
Imam (as) said: 'Pray in it, for there is merit in it, and my father (as) used to command this.'"
